steps.note: Roll the app to store '' (not NULL) as the email of guest orders. The deploy waits for the rollout, so afterwards no pod writes NULL emails any more.

Add CHECK (email IS NOT NULL) NOT VALID: enforced for new writes from now on, no scan of existing rows. Needs a brief ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock, so take it with a short lock_timeout and retry, never queueing app traffic behind it for long.
steps.sql: SET lock_timeout = '500ms'; DO $$ BEGIN FOR i IN 1..120 LOOP BEGIN ALTER TABLE orders ADD CONSTRAINT orders_email_not_null CHECK (email IS NOT NULL) NOT VALID; RETURN; EXCEPTION WHEN lock_not_available THEN PERFORM pg_sleep(0.5); END; END LOOP; RAISE EXCEPTION 'could not lock orders to add constraint'; END $$;

steps.note: Backfill: set email = '' on the existing guest orders, in id ranges of 50,000 with a commit after each batch, so locks and transactions stay short.
steps.sql: SET statement_timeout = 0; DO $$ DECLARE lo bigint := 0; hi bigint; BEGIN SELECT max(id) INTO hi FROM orders; WHILE lo <= hi LOOP UPDATE orders SET email = '' WHERE id > lo AND id <= lo + 50000 AND email IS NULL; COMMIT; lo := lo + 50000; END LOOP; END $$;

steps.note: Clean up the dead row versions left by the backfill.
Validate the constraint: one scan of the table under SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE, which does not block reads or writes. Fails if any NULL email is left.
steps.sql: SET statement_timeout = 0; SET lock_timeout = '60s'; ALTER TABLE orders VALIDATE CONSTRAINT orders_email_not_null;

steps.note: SET NOT NULL: Postgres uses the validated CHECK constraint as proof and skips the table scan, so the ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock is only held for an instant. Short lock_timeout with retries.
steps.sql: SET lock_timeout = '500ms'; DO $$ BEGIN FOR i IN 1..120 LOOP BEGIN ALTER TABLE orders ALTER COLUMN email SET NOT NULL; RETURN; EXCEPTION WHEN lock_not_available THEN PERFORM pg_sleep(0.5); END; END LOOP; RAISE EXCEPTION 'could not lock orders to set NOT NULL'; END $$;

steps.note: Drop the now redundant CHECK constraint (same short-lock retry).
steps.sql: SET lock_timeout = '500ms'; DO $$ BEGIN FOR i IN 1..120 LOOP BEGIN ALTER TABLE orders DROP CONSTRAINT orders_email_not_null; RETURN; EXCEPTION WHEN lock_not_available THEN PERFORM pg_sleep(0.5); END; END LOOP; RAISE EXCEPTION 'could not lock orders to drop constraint'; END $$;

steps.note: Check the result: orders.email is NOT NULL.
steps.sql: DO $$ BEGIN IF NOT (SELECT attnotnull FROM pg_attribute WHERE attrelid = 'orders'::regclass AND attname = 'email') THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'orders.email is still nullable'; END IF; END $$;
